subject: encountered ERROR when using stan to simulate/fit ODE

messages.author: 5c24954f6be9e2ef
messages.subject: encountered ERROR when using stan to simulate/fit ODE
parts:
I am trying to simulate an ODE system with measurement error. Attached is the stan file I used in the simulation. Below are the parameters used in my code. Note X_r contains the fixed parameters for defining the ODE system. theta contains the parameters I would like to estimate from observed data with measurement error.

```{r}
library(rstan)
n <- 4 ## number of layers
theta <- c(kpwa = log(2)/50, kpse = log(2)/50, Kd = 50)
Zs <- 2
Zsed <- rep(Zs/n,n)
x_r <- c(rhob=2.05,theta=0.5,Zw=5,Dp=0.05,delta=1,Zsed)
y0 <- c(1,rep(0,n))
ts <- seq(0,100,by=10)
T <- length(ts)
t0 <- 0
## sm <- stan_model(file="RPest/stan/WS4.stan")
swData <- stan(file="RPest/stan/WS4.stan",data=c("T","y0","t0","ts","theta"),chains=1,iter=1,algorithm="Fixed_param")
```

I got the error as below:

Error : integrate_ode(d): continuous data[1] is 1.#QNAN, but must be finite!
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done


Not sure where it went wrong.

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] encountered ERROR when using stan to simulate/fit ODE
parts:
Hi Zhenglei,

The issue is with the data you are passing into the integrate_ode() function. It's the x_r argument here:
  y_hat <- integrate_ode(sw4, y0, t0, ts, theta, x_r, x_i);

You've declared x_r as transformed parameters, but never set any of the values, so they are initialized to NaN (not a number... Windows prints it as 1.#QNAN). This might be as simple as filling in the values for x_r[], your data.



Daniel

             real[] theta,
             real[] x_r,

  dydt[4] <- -x_r[5]*theta[2]*y[4]+2*x_r[4]*fdiss/(x_r[7]+x_r[8])*(y[3]/x_r[7]-y[4]/x_r[8])-2*x_r[4]*fdiss/(x_r[8]+x_r[9])*(y[4]/x_r[8]-y[5]/x_r[9]);
  dydt[5] <- -x_r[5]*theta[2]*y[5]+2*x_r[4]*fdiss/(x_r[8]+x_r[9])*(y[4]/x_r[8]-y[5]/x_r[9]);
  return dydt;
  }
}

}
transformed data {

}

}

// add measurement error

    y_hat[t,2] <- y_hat[t,2] + normal_rng(0,0.1);
    y_hat[t,3] <- y_hat[t,3] + normal_rng(0,0.1);
    y_hat[t,4] <- y_hat[t,4] + normal_rng(0,0.1);
    y_hat[t,5] <- y_hat[t,5] + normal_rng(0,0.1);
  }
}


I got new error message:


Error : integrate_ode(d): initial time is 0, but must be less than 0
error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done

Are there again obvious explanations?

Best,
Zhenglei

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] encountered ERROR when using stan to simulate/fit ODE
parts:
Yes, there is. My guess is that your initial time, t0, is 0.

The ts have to be sorted, unique, and all greater than t0, in this case 0. We need to document it better in the manual and the right thing to do is to relax that condition in the underlying C++ code.

Just in case you're wondering, the integrate_ode() call uses the implementation of the Runge-Kutta Dormand-Prince 5 method in Boost's ODEINT package. For the first implementation of our wrapper function, integrate_ode(), we followed the requirements of the Boost solver, which requires sorted, unique times which do not include the initial time. In order for us to make the Stan function more flexible, it's a lot of bookkeeping that can be done in C++, it's just tricky. (perhaps a little trickier than it looks on the surface because we're having to track the gradients and we do this with a coupled system. see the arXiv'ed math paper for details)

So, in short, you can set the 2nd to the nth element of y_hat by dropping the first ts. The first element of y_hat should be y0. Hopefully that helps.


Daniel
